newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE MATCHES.

text.p: Analysis of key elements in Wednesday's European Cup Champions' League matches:
Group A
Glasgow Rangers (Scotland) v Auxerre (France)

Rangers, beaten 3-0 by Grasshopper Zurich two weeks ago, will be without suspended Yugoslav defender Gordan Petric and Scotland striker Ally McCoist, who has a calf injury. Scotland midfielder Stuart McCall is also doubtful with a thigh injury. Australian Craig Moore is likely to replace Petric. Danish forward Brian Laudrup missed a League Cup game last week but returned for Saturday's 4-1 league win over Kilmarnock.

Auxerre, beaten 1-0 at home by Ajax Amsterdam in their Champions' League opener, will be without their two first-choice central defenders. Captain and sweeper Franck Silvestre has a shoulder injury and Australian Ned Zelic has knee problems. Striker Lilian Laslandes suffered a groin injury in a league game last week and there will be a late decision on his fitness.
Ajax Amsterdam (Netherlands) v Grasshopper Zurich (Switzerland)

Ajax will be without Nigerian winger Tijani Babangida (knee injury). Defender Winston Bogarde has a sore foot and is an unlikely starter. Skipper Danny Blind returns from injury but fellow internationals John Veldman, Richard Witschge, Patrick Kluivert and Peter Hoekstra are all still sidelined by injury.

Grasshopper have seven injured players, including Euro 96 striker Kubilay Turkyilmaz who has a strained calf muscle but is expected to play. The other injured players are Mats Gren, Joel Magnin and Harald Gamperle, all in the starting line-up in this month's 3-0 win over Rangers, and Tomasz Rzasa, Alain Geiger and Nestor Subiat.
Group B
Steaua Bucharest (Romania) v Borussia Dortmund (Germany)

Steaua will be without four key players. Forward Adrian Ilie and sweeper Marius Baciu are suspended after being sent off, Ilie in a qualifier against Brugge and Baciu in the 4-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid two weeks ago. Striker Marius Lacatus is recovering from an old muscle injury and central defender Daniel Prodan is also injured. Steaua trainer Dumitru Dumitriu said Ilie would be replaced by his brother Sabin, top scorer in Romania this season with seven goals in seven matches.

Borussia Dortmund, 2-1 winners over Widzew Lodz in the opening Champions' League series but crushed 5-1 by Borussia Moenchengladbach in the German league on Saturday, welcome back from injury Brazilian defender Julio Cesar and midfielder Rene Tretschok. But international midfielders Steffen Freund and Knut Reinhardt (both knee injuries), striker Karlheinz Riedle (neck injury) and Ibrahim Tanko (torn hamstring) are sidelined.
Widzew Lodz (Poland) v Atletico Madrid (Spain)

Widzew gave themselves a boost on Saturday when they came from behind with two goals in the final 15 minutes to score a 2-1 away win over Wisla Krakow and move within a point of the three leading clubs in the Polish first division. Widzew coach Franciszek Smuda said his team had not been at full strength because he was saving some players for the Atletico clash.

Atletico will be without suspended playmaker Jose Luis Caminero. Midfielder Juan Vizcaino and forward Leonardo Biagini are both doubtful because of injury. Coach Radomir Antic was happy not to see any additions to Atletico's already lengthy injury list after Saturday's 3-0 league win over Logrones.
Group C
Manchester United (England) v Rapid Vienna (Austria)

Denmark goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel and England defender Gary Pallister should win fitness battles. Pallister has been suffering from a knee injury and Schmeichel is getting over a virus. Striker Andy Cole may make his first appearance in the starting line-up this season in preference to Norway's Gunnar Ole Solskjaer. The return of combative Irish midfielder Roy Keane, who missed the 1-0 defeat by Juventus two weeks ago, should be a boost.

Rapid Vienna's midfield will be significantly weakened by the absence of Christian Prosenik, who injured his right knee in Saturday's 2-0 Austrian league win over Admira Wacker. He will be replaced by Czech player Roman Pivarnik. Polish midfielder Krzysztof Ratajczyk, who missed the 1-1 draw with Fenerbahce two weeks ago with a fractured ankle, is fit again.
Fenerbahce (Turkey) v Juventus (Italy)

Fenerbahce will be without suspended Bulgarian forward Emil Kostadinov. Key midfielder Tayfun Korkut may also be ruled out. He was taken to hospital after a fit of vomiting following a 5-1 league win over Zeytinburnuspor at the weekend and put on a serum drip. International goalkeeper Rustu Recber is nursing a strained muscle but the team doctor expects him to be fit.

Reigning European champions Juventus share the lead in the Italian first division after a 2-1 away win over Perugia on Sunday but coach Marcello Lippi is set to shuffle his line-up. "The whole point of a large squad is to make changes and to rotate the players," he said. Christian Vieri, dropped against Perugia, returns to the attack in place of Nicola Amoruso, alongside Croat Alen Boksic and Alessandro Del Piero.
Group D
Porto (Portugal) v Gothenburg (Sweden)

Brazilian striker Artur Oliveira and defenders Fernando Mendes and Sergio Conceicao have slight injuries but should be fit to play for Porto, surprise 3-2 conquerors of favourites AC Milan two weeks ago. They were injured in a 1-0 league win over Salgueiros at the weekend. Top league scorer Domingos Oliveira is still recovering from a knee operation which is likely to keep him out of action until the end of the year. Austrian midfielder Arnold Wetl, a recent signing, is ineligible.

Gothenburg midfielder Stefan Pettersson returns after a thigh muscle injury but defender Jonas Olsson is out with back problems. The Swedish premier league leaders lost 1-0 away to modest Orebro at the weekend but stayed top of the table with just two games to play before the end of the season.
Rosenborg (Norway) v AC Milan (Italy)

Rosenborg, Norwegian elite division champions, do not expect major changes to the team which beat Gothenburg 3-2 in Sweden two weeks ago. Top scorer Harald Brattbakk will play and there are no new injuries. "There won't be any surprises. We're looking forward to the match and we are feeling confident," a club spokesman said.

Milan coach Oscar Washington Tabarez hopes injured captain Franco Baresi will recover in time to replace fellow veteran defender Pietro Vierchowod, who is cup-tied. If Baresi fails to make it Tabarez can field either Filippo Galli or Frenchman Marcel Desailly alongside Alessandro Costacurta, with Dutchman Edgar Davids replacing Desailly in midfield. Roberto Baggio is likely to be left out of an attack featuring Liberian George Weah, Montenegrin Dejan Savicevic and Marco Simone.
